Sudova Vyshnya Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Jewish presence in Sudova Vyshnya dates to at least the mid-16th century, with an independent community established by the late 18th century that maintained both a synagogue and a cemetery. The population peaked near 1,300 (about 30 percent of the town) by 1890, and Zionist organizations remained active through the interwar years even as numbers declined to around 900 by 1931. After the town's occupation in June 1941, some 450 Jews were expelled to the Janowska concentration camp in April 1942, and the rest were deported to the Belzec extermination camp or the Yavoriv ghetto later that year; the cemetery itself, documented on maps as early as the 1850s, is now occupied by an agricultural warehouse.
